external_evidence: Only one artifact fails (xlwings macOS wheel) while numpy from the same GCP Artifact Registry repo installs fine, and the 403 comes from the registry's download endpoint (artifacts-downloads/.../downloads/***), which is a Google Artifact Registry access or availability decision rather than uv behaviour. This points to the registry or its per-file permissions, not uv.

possible_duplicates.reason: Same symptom: uv pip install returns 403 from a private cloud-hosted PyPI-style index (S3-backed), closed as a question. Symptom match only; root cause not verified.
Same symptom: 403 errors when uv fetches from private artifact registries via extra index URLs with JSON-key auth. Symptom match only; root cause not verified.

rationale: The reporter labels this a bug, but the decisive clue is that a single wheel returns 403 from the Google Artifact Registry download endpoint while other packages from the same repo install, which points to a registry-side permission or missing-file problem outside uv, so I classed it as a question and likely_external. The platform is also inconsistent (Windows reporter, macOS wheel) and no verbose output or credential check was given, so needs_mre is true. Search found 2025 and 11244 as 403-from-private-index symptom matches, and 16662 as a related request for clearer 403 messages. The docs search returned docs/guides/integration/google.md, which I did not open because the tool-call budget was used up.
